questions.question: ​In a trapezium, one diagonal divides the other in the ratio 2 ∶ 7. If the length of the larger of the two parallel sides is 42 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of the other parallel side?
questions.questionHtml: ​In a trapezium, one diagonal divides the other in the ratio 2 ∶ 7. If the length of the larger of the two parallel sides is 42 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of the other parallel side?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a trapezium, the ratio of the lengths of the parallel sides is equal to the ratio in which the diagonals divide each other.

Ratio of parallel sides = Ratio of diagonal segments = 2 : 7

Given larger parallel side (7 parts) = 42 cm

1 part = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 cm

Smaller parallel side (2 parts) = 2 × 6 = 12 cm

∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of segments of diagonals = 2 : 7

Length of larger parallel side = 42 cm

Formula Used:

In a trapezium ABCD with AB || CD and diagonals intersecting at O, ΔAOB ∼ ΔCOD (by AAA similarity). Therefore, AB/CD = AO/CO = BO/DO.

Calculations:

⇒ Let the parallel sides be a and b, where b = 42 cm.

⇒ According to the similarity property: a / b = 2 / 7

⇒ a / 42 = 2 / 7

⇒ a = (2 × 42) ÷ 7

⇒ a = 2 × 6

⇒ a = 12 cm

∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.

Additional Information

Area of Trapezium

The area of a trapezium is calculated as 1/2 × (sum of parallel sides) × height, or Area = 1/2 × (a + b) × h.

Median of a Trapezium

The line segment joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides is called the median, and its length is the average of the parallel sides: Median = (a + b) ÷ 2.

Similarity Property

The triangles formed by the intersection of diagonals and the parallel sides (top and bottom triangles) are always similar by AAA criteria because of alternate interior angles.

questions.question: The area enclosed between the circumferences of two concentric circles is 16π cm 2 and their radii are in the ratio 5 ∶ 3. What is the area of the outer circle?
questions.questionHtml: The area enclosed between the circumferences of two concentric circles is 16π cm2 and their radii are in the ratio 5 ∶ 3. What is the area of the outer circle?

options.html: 9π cm2
16π cm2
25π cm2
36π cm2

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of radii (R : r) = 5 : 3

Ratio of areas (R2 : r2) = 52 : 32 = 25 : 9

Difference in area units = 25 − 9 = 16 units

Given, 16 units = 16π cm2 ⇒ 1 unit = π cm2

Area of outer circle = 25 units = 25 × π = 25π cm2

∴ The correct answer is 25π cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Area between circles = 16π cm2

Ratio of radii R : r = 5 : 3

Formula Used:

Area of circle = πr2

Area of ring = π(R2 − r2)

Calculations:

Let the radii be 5x and 3x.

⇒ π[(5x)2 − (3x)2] = 16π

⇒ 25x2 − 9x2 = 16

⇒ 16x2 = 16

⇒ x2 = 1

⇒ x = 1

⇒ Outer radius (R) = 5 × 1 = 5 cm

⇒ Area of outer circle = π × (5)2

⇒ Area = 25π cm2

∴ The correct answer is 25π cm2.

Additional Information

Concentric Circles

Circles having the same center but different radii are called concentric circles. The region between them is called an annulus or ring.

Circumference Difference

The difference between the circumferences of two concentric circles is given by 2π(R − r), which is also 2π times the width of the ring.

Area Scaling Rule

If the radii of two circles are in the ratio a : b, then their areas are in the ratio a2 : b2.

questions.question: Pure milk costs Rs. 16 per litre. After adding water the milkman sells the mixture at Rs. 15 per litre and thereby makes a profit of 25%. In what respective ratio does he mix milk with water?
questions.questionHtml: Pure milk costs Rs. 16 per litre. After adding water the milkman sells the mixture at Rs. 15 per litre and thereby makes a profit of 25%. In what respective ratio does he mix milk with water?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

CP of mixture = SP ÷ (1 + Profit%) = 15 ÷ 1.25 = ₹12.

By Alligation: (Milk CP − Mean CP) : (Mean CP − Water CP) gives the ratio.

Ratio of Milk : Water = (Mean − Water) : (Milk − Mean) = (12 − 0) : (16 − 12).

Ratio = 12 : 4 = 3 : 1.

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost Price (CP) of pure milk = ₹16/litre

Selling Price (SP) of mixture = ₹15/litre

Profit percentage = 25%

Cost Price (CP) of water = ₹0/litre (assumed)

Formula Used:

CP of mixture = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 + Profit%]

Calculations:

⇒ Mean CP = (15 × 100) ÷ (100 + 25)

⇒ Mean CP = (15 × 100) ÷ 125

⇒ Mean CP = 1500 ÷ 125 = ₹12 per litre

⇒ Using Rule of Alligation:

⇒ (Quantity of Milk) / (Quantity of Water) = (Mean CP − CP of Water) / (CP of Milk − Mean CP)

⇒ Ratio = (12 − 0) / (16 − 12)

⇒ Ratio = 12 / 4

⇒ Ratio = 3 / 1

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

It is used to find the ratio in which two ingredients at given prices must be mixed to produce a mixture at a specific price. Ratio = (Cheaper diff) : (Dearer diff).

Cost of Water

In mixture problems involving milk and water, the cost price of water is always considered ₹0 per unit unless specified otherwise in the question.

Effective CP with Profit

To apply alligation when a profit is made, always convert the Selling Price of the mixture back to the Cost Price using the formula CP = SP × 100 / (100 + P%).

questions.question: Simplify the given expression using VBODMAS rule: \(65-40\%\ of\left(200\div 5\times 3-6\right)+\overline{16-12}-20\div 4\) ?
questions.questionHtml:
Simplify the given expression using VBODMAS rule:

\(65-40\%\ of\left(200\div 5\times 3-6\right)+\overline{16-12}-20\div 4\) ?
questions.solution:
Given:

\(65 - 40\% \text{ of } (200 \div 5 \times 3 - 6) + \overline{16-12} - 20 \div 4\) = ?

Formula used:

VBODMAS Rule (Vinculum, Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

Calculations:

\(65 - 40\% \text{ of } (200 \div 5 \times 3 - 6) + \overline{16-12} - 20 \div 4\) = ?

⇒ ? = \(65 - 40\% \text{ of } (40 \times 3 - 6) + 4 - 5\)

⇒ ? = \(65 - 40\% \text{ of } (120 - 6) - 1\)

⇒ ? = \(65 - 40\% \text{ of } 114 - 1\)

⇒ ? = \(65 - (0.4 \times 114) - 1\)

⇒ ? = \(65 - 45.6 - 1\)

⇒ ? = \(19.4 - 1\)

⇒ ? = 18.4

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: Due to a fall of 20% in the rates of wheat a man can buy 10 kg more than before for Rs 600. What is the decreased rate per kg?
questions.questionHtml: Due to a fall of 20% in the rates of wheat a man can buy 10 kg more than before for Rs 600. What is the decreased rate per kg?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Decreased Rate = (Reduction % × Total Expenditure) ÷ Extra Quantity

Reduction = 20% of ₹600 = ₹120

This ₹120 is the cost of the extra 10 kg wheat at the new rate.

Decreased Rate = 120 ÷ 10 = ₹12.00 per kg

∴ The correct answer is ₹12.00.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Expenditure = ₹600

Reduction in Price = 20%

Increase in Quantity = 10 kg

Let the original rate per kg be x.

⇒ Original quantity = 600 ÷ x

⇒ Decreased rate = 80% of x = 0.8x

⇒ New quantity = 600 ÷ (0.8x) = 750 ÷ x

⇒ Difference in quantity = (750 ÷ x) − (600 ÷ x) = 10

⇒ 150 ÷ x = 10

⇒ x = 150 ÷ 10 = ₹15 (Original Rate)

⇒ Decreased rate = 0.8 × 15 = ₹12.00

∴ The correct answer is ₹12.00.

Additional Information

Price and Consumption Relation

When expenditure is constant, Price is inversely proportional to Consumption (P ∝ 1/C). If price decreases by r%, consumption must increase to keep expenditure same.

Direct Formula for Original Rate

Original Rate = (r × E) ÷ [(100 − r) × q], where r = % reduction, E = expenditure, q = extra quantity.

Direct Formula for Decreased Rate

Decreased Rate = (r × E) ÷ (100 × q). This gives the new price per unit directly after the percentage change.

questions.question: A solid metallic cuboid of dimensions 12 cm × 54 cm × 72 cm is melted and converted into 8 cubes of the same size. What is the sum of the lateral surface areas (in cm 2 ) of 2 such cubes?
questions.questionHtml: A solid metallic cuboid of dimensions 12 cm × 54 cm × 72 cm is melted and converted into 8 cubes of the same size. What is the sum of the lateral surface areas (in cm<sup>2</sup>) of 2 such cubes?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Volume of 8 cubes = Volume of Cuboid

8 × a3 = 12 × 54 × 72

a3 = 12 × 54 × 9 ⇒ a3 = 5832 ⇒ a = 18 cm

Lateral Surface Area of 2 cubes = 2 × (4a2) = 8 × 182

Total LSA = 8 × 324 = 2592 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 2592 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given: Dimensions of cuboid = 12 cm × 54 cm × 72 cm, Number of cubes = 8.

Formula: Volume of cuboid = L × B × H; Volume of cube = a3; LSA of cube = 4a2.

⇒ Volume of cuboid = 12 × 54 × 72 = 46656 cm3.

⇒ Volume of 8 cubes = 46656 cm3.

⇒ Volume of 1 cube = 46656 ÷ 8 = 5832 cm3.

⇒ a3 = 5832 ⇒ a = √35832 = 18 cm.

⇒ Lateral Surface Area (LSA) of 1 cube = 4a2.

⇒ LSA of 1 cube = 4 × (18)2 = 4 × 324 = 1296 cm2.

⇒ Sum of LSAs of 2 cubes = 2 × 1296 = 2592 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 2592 cm2.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cube and Cuboid

TSA of a cube = 6a2 and TSA of a cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl).

Diagonal of Cube and Cuboid

Length of the longest rod (diagonal) in a cube = a√3 and in a cuboid = √(l2 + b2 + h2).

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

LSA refers to the area of the vertical faces only. For a cube, it is 4a2; for a cuboid, it is 2h(l + b).

questions.question: A well with inner radius 3 m, is dug 6 m deep. The soil taken out of it has been spread evenly all around it to a width of 2 m to form an embankment. The height (in m) of the embankment is:
questions.questionHtml: A well with inner radius 3 m, is dug 6 m deep. The soil taken out of it has been spread evenly all around it to a width of 2 m to form an embankment. The height (in m) of the embankment is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Inner radius (r) = 3 m, Depth (h) = 6 m, Embankment Width = 2 m

Outer radius (R) = r + width = 3 + 2 = 5 m

Height of embankment (H) = (r2 × h) / (R2 − r2)

H = (32 × 6) / (52 − 32)

H = 54 / (25 − 9) = 54 / 16 = 27 / 8 = 3 3/8 m

∴ The correct answer is 3 3/8 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Inner radius of well (r) = 3 m

Depth of well (h) = 6 m

Width of embankment = 2 m

Formula Used:

Volume of Cylinder = π × r2 × h

Volume of Embankment (Hollow Cylinder) = π × (R2 − r2) × H

Calculations:

⇒ Volume of soil taken out = π × r2 × h

⇒ Volume of soil = π × 32 × 6 = 54π m3

⇒ Outer radius of embankment (R) = Inner radius + width = 3 + 2 = 5 m

⇒ Volume of embankment = π × (R2 − r2) × H

⇒ Volume of embankment = π × (52 − 32) × H = π × (25 − 9) × H = 16πH

⇒ Volume of soil = Volume of embankment

⇒ 54π = 16πH

⇒ H = 54 / 16 = 27 / 8

⇒ H = 3 3/8 m

∴ The correct answer is 3 3/8 m.

Additional Information

Volume of Cylinder

The volume of a solid cylinder is given by V = πr2h, where r is the radius and h is the height.

Volume of Hollow Cylinder (Embankment)

The volume of a hollow cylinder is the difference between the volumes of the outer and inner cylinders: V = π(R2 − r2)h.

Conservation of Volume

When an object is reshaped (like soil from a hole used to build a platform), the total volume remains constant.

questions.question: Find the value of \(\frac{1}{4\frac{2}{7}}+\frac{1}{3\frac{11}{13}}+ \frac{1}{\left(\frac{5}{9}\right) }\)
questions.questionHtml: Find the value of \(\frac{1}{4\frac{2}{7}}+\frac{1}{3\frac{11}{13}}+ \frac{1}{\left(\frac{5}{9}\right) }\)
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{1}{4\frac{2}{7}}+\frac{1}{3\frac{11}{13}}+ \frac{1}{\left(\frac{5}{9}\right) }\)

Formula used:

a b/c = (a × c + b) / c

1 / (a/b) = b/a

Calculation:

\(\frac{1}{4\frac{2}{7}}+\frac{1}{3\frac{11}{13}}+ \frac{1}{\left(\frac{5}{9}\right) }\)

⇒ \(\frac{1}{\frac{30}{7}}+\frac{1}{\frac{50}{13}}+ \frac{9}{5}\)

⇒ \(\frac{7}{30}+\frac{13}{50}+ \frac{9}{5}\)

⇒ \(\frac{(7 \times 5) + (13 \times 3) + (9 \times 30)}{150}\)

⇒ \(\frac{35 + 39 + 270}{150}\)

⇒ \(\frac{344}{150}\)

⇒ \(\frac{172}{75}\)

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: If the price of petrol increases by 25% and Sunita intends to spend only an additional 12.5% on petrol, by what percent should she reduced the quantity of petrol purchased (nearest to an integer)?
questions.questionHtml: If the price of petrol increases by 25% and Sunita intends to spend only an additional 12.5% on petrol, by what percent should she reduced the quantity of petrol purchased (nearest to an integer)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

New Quantity Ratio = (100 + % Expenditure change) ÷ (100 + % Price change)

New Quantity Ratio = 112.5 ÷ 125 = 0.9

Percentage Reduction = (1 − 0.9) × 100 = 10%

∴ The correct answer is 10%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Increase in Price = 25%

Increase in Expenditure = 12.5%

Formula: Expenditure = Price × Quantity

Let initial Price = ₹100 and initial Quantity = 100 units.

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 100 × 100 = ₹10,000

New Price = 100 + 25% of 100 = ₹125

New Expenditure = 10,000 + 12.5% of 10,000 = ₹11,250

⇒ New Quantity = New Expenditure ÷ New Price

⇒ New Quantity = 11,250 ÷ 125 = 90 units

Reduction in Quantity = 100 − 90 = 10 units

⇒ Percentage Reduction = (10 ÷ 100) × 100 = 10%

∴ The correct answer is 10%.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Formula

Total % change in Expenditure = x + y + (xy/100), where x is % change in price and y is % change in quantity.

Constant Expenditure Rule

If expenditure remains constant, the quantity is inversely proportional to the price: Q1/Q2 = P2/P1.

Price-Consumption Relation

If price increases by r%, consumption must be reduced by [r/(100+r)] × 100% to keep expenditure same.

questions.question: From the top of a tower, the angle of depression of the top of a 10 m high building is 60°. If the distance between the tower and the building is 50√3 m, find the height of the tower.
questions.questionHtml: From the top of a tower, the angle of depression of the top of a 10 m high building is 60°. If the distance between the tower and the building is 50√3 m, find the height of the tower.
questions.solution:
Given: height of building = 10 m, angle of depression = 60º, distance = 50√3 m.

Let height of tower be h meters.

tan(60º) = (h - 10) / (50√3)

√3 = (h - 10) / (50√3), h - 10 = 50√3 × √3

h - 10 = 150, h = 160 m.

questions.question: The price of coffee increased by 35% and then decreased by 20%. If a man reduces his consumption of coffee by 4.5%, then what is the percentage change in his expenditure?
questions.questionHtml: The price of coffee increased by 35% and then decreased by 20%. If a man reduces his consumption of coffee by 4.5%, then what is the percentage change in his expenditure?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net Price change = 35 − 20 − (35 × 20 ÷ 100) = 8% increase.

Net Expenditure change = 8 − 4.5 − (8 × 4.5 ÷ 100).

⇒ 3.5 − 0.36 = 3.14%.

Positive result indicates an increase.

∴ The correct answer is Increase by 3.14%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Price increase = 35%

Subsequent Price decrease = 20%

Consumption decrease = 4.5%

Formula Used:

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

Net Change % = x + y + (xy ÷ 100)

Calculations:

⇒ Let initial Price = 100 and initial Consumption = 100.

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 100 × 100 = 10,000.

⇒ Price after 35% increase = 100 + 35 = 135.

⇒ Price after 20% decrease on 135 = 135 − (20% of 135) = 135 − 27 = 108.

⇒ New Consumption after 4.5% decrease = 100 − 4.5 = 95.5.

⇒ New Expenditure = New Price × New Consumption = 108 × 95.5.

⇒ New Expenditure = 10,314.

⇒ Percentage change = [(10,314 − 10,000) ÷ 10,000] × 100.

⇒ Percentage change = (314 ÷ 10,000) × 100 = 3.14%.

⇒ Since the value is positive, it is an increase.

∴ The correct answer is Increase by 3.14%.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Formula

When a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net change is given by [a + b + (ab ÷ 100)]%.

Expenditure Relationship

If Expenditure = Price × Consumption, then the net percentage change in expenditure is the successive result of price change % and consumption change %.

Base Change Rule

If Price increases by x%, then to keep expenditure constant, consumption must decrease by [x ÷ (100 + x)] × 100%.

questions.question: What is that greatest four-digit number which when divided by 3 and 4 leaves remainder 2 in each case?
questions.questionHtml: What is that greatest four-digit number which when divided by 3 and 4 leaves remainder 2 in each case?
questions.solution:
LCM of 3 and 4 = 12 and the largest four-digit number = 9999

Largest four-digit number divisible by 12 = 9999 - (9999 mod 12) = 9999 - 3 = 9996

Adding remainder = 9996 + 2 = 9998

questions.question: There is a rectangular tank 2.1 m long, 1.5 m wide and half filled with water. By how much will the depth of water increase by pouring 630 liters of water into that tank?
questions.questionHtml: There is a rectangular tank 2.1 m long, 1.5 m wide and half filled with water. By how much will the depth of water increase by pouring 630 liters of water into that tank?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Base Area = Length × Width = 2.1 × 1.5 = 3.15 m2

Volume of water added = 630 Liters = 0.63 m3 (since 1000 L = 1 m3)

Rise in water depth (h) = Volume added ÷ Base Area = 0.63 ÷ 3.15 = 0.2 m

Converting to decimeters: 0.2 m = 0.2 × 10 = 2 dm

∴ The correct answer is 2 dm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length (L) = 2.1 m

Width (W) = 1.5 m

Volume of water added = 630 liters

Formula Used:

Volume of cuboid = Length × Width × Height

Increase in Volume = Length × Width × Increase in Depth

Calculations:

⇒ 1 m3 = 1000 liters

⇒ Volume of water added (V) = 630 ÷ 1000 = 0.63 m3

⇒ Base Area of the tank = L × W = 2.1 × 1.5 = 3.15 m2

⇒ Increase in depth (h) = Volume ÷ Base Area

⇒ h = 0.63 ÷ 3.15

⇒ h = 0.2 m

⇒ Since 1 m = 10 dm (decimeters)

⇒ h = 0.2 × 10 = 2 dm

∴ The correct answer is 2 dm.

Additional Information

Volume and Capacity Units

The capacity of a container is often measured in liters. Note that 1 liter = 1000 cm3 = 1 dm3, and 1000 liters = 1 m3.

Metric Length Conversions

1 meter (m) = 10 decimeters (dm) = 100 centimeters (cm) = 1000 millimeters (mm).

Volume of a Cuboid

The volume of any prism with a uniform cross-section, like a cuboid, is calculated as Area of Base × Height.

questions.question: The marked price of a TV is ₹50,000. The difference between a discount of 30% and two successive discounts of 25% and 6% on this deal is:
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of a TV is ₹50,000. The difference between a discount of 30% and two successive discounts of 25% and 6% on this deal is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Equivalent percentage of successive discounts 25% and 6% = 25 + 6 − (25 × 6)/100 = 29.5%

Difference between 30% single discount and 29.5% successive discount = 30% − 29.5% = 0.5%

Difference in amount = 0.5% of ₹50,000

⇒ (0.5/100) × 50000 = ₹250

∴ The correct answer is ₹250.

Alternate Method

Given:

Marked Price (MP) = ₹50,000

Discount 1 = 30%

Successive Discounts = 25% and 6%

Formula Used:

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − Discount%/100)

Calculations:

Case 1 (Single discount of 30%):

⇒ SP1 = 50000 × (1 − 30/100) = 50000 × 0.70 = ₹35,000

Case 2 (Successive discounts of 25% and 6%):

⇒ SP2 = 50000 × (1 − 25/100) × (1 − 6/100)

⇒ SP2 = 50000 × 0.75 × 0.94

⇒ SP2 = 37500 × 0.94 = ₹35,250

Difference:

The difference in discounts is identical to the difference in Selling Prices.

⇒ Difference = SP2 − SP1

⇒ Difference = 35250 − 35000 = ₹250

∴ The correct answer is ₹250.

Additional Information

Successive Discounts

When a discount is given on the previously discounted price, it is called a successive discount. The equivalent discount of D1% and D2% is given by the formula: [D1 + D2 − (D1 × D2)/100]%.

Marked Price (MP)

It is the label price of an article. Any discount offered by a merchant is always calculated on the Marked Price, not on the Cost Price.

Single Discount vs Successive Discount

A single flat discount equal to the sum of successive discount percentages is always greater than the successive discount combined. For example, a flat 30% discount is always more beneficial to a buyer than successive discounts of 25% and 5%.

questions.question: A waiter's income consists of his salary and tips. During one week, his tips were 5/4 of his salary. What fraction of his income came from tips?
questions.questionHtml: A waiter's income consists of his salary and tips. During one week, his tips were 5/4 of his salary. What fraction of his income came from tips?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Tips to Salary = 5 : 4

Total Income = Tips + Salary = 5 + 4 = 9 units

Fraction of income from tips = Tips ÷ Total Income = 5/9

∴ The correct answer is 5/9.

Alternate Method

Given:

Tips = 5/4 × Salary

Total Income = Salary + Tips

Formula:

Fraction of tips = Tips ÷ (Salary + Tips)

Let Salary = 4x

⇒ Tips = 5/4 × 4x = 5x

⇒ Total Income = 4x + 5x = 9x

⇒ Fraction of income from tips = 5x ÷ 9x

⇒ Fraction = 5/9

∴ The correct answer is 5/9.

Additional Information

Ratio to Fraction

If the ratio of two parts A and B is a:b, the fraction of A in the whole (A+B) is a/(a+b) and the fraction of B is b/(a+b).

Percentage Calculation

To convert the fraction of tips into a percentage, multiply by 100. Example: (5/9) × 100 ≈ 55.55%.

Proportion Rule

If A = (m/n) × B, then the ratio A:B is m:n. Here, Tips = (5/4) × Salary, so Tips:Salary = 5:4.

questions.question: The average weight of L, M and N is 93 kg. If the average weight of L and M be 89 kg and that of M and N be 96.5 kg, then the weight (in kg) of M is ______
questions.questionHtml: The average weight of L, M and N is 93 kg. If the average weight of L and M be 89 kg and that of M and N be 96.5 kg, then the weight (in kg) of M is ______
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Weight of common person (M) = [Sum of individual pairs] − [Total sum]

M = 2 × (AvgL+M + AvgM+N) − 3 × (AvgL+M+N)

M = 2 × (89 + 96.5) − 3 × 93

M = 2 × 185.5 − 279 = 371 − 279 = 92 kg.

∴ The correct answer is 92 kg.

Alternate Method

Given:

Average weight of (L, M, N) = 93 kg

Average weight of (L, M) = 89 kg

Average weight of (M, N) = 96.5 kg

Formula Used:

Total Weight = Average Weight × Number of persons

Calculations:

⇒ Total weight of (L + M + N) = 93 × 3 = 279 kg --- (Eq. 1)

⇒ Total weight of (L + M) = 89 × 2 = 178 kg --- (Eq. 2)

⇒ Total weight of (M + N) = 96.5 × 2 = 193 kg --- (Eq. 3)

⇒ Weight of M = (Total weight of L + M) + (Total weight of M + N) − (Total weight of L + M + N)

⇒ Weight of M = 178 + 193 − 279

⇒ Weight of M = 371 − 279

⇒ Weight of M = 92 kg

∴ The correct answer is 92 kg.

Additional Information

Average Concept

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).

Deviation Method

If the average of n terms is A, and one term is part of two overlapping subsets, the term = A + ∑(Deviations). This avoids large multiplications.

Weighted Average

Combined Average = (n1x1 + n2x2) ÷ (n1 + n2), where n is the number of items and x is the average of each group.

questions.question: Pipe A and pipe B can fill a tank alone in 6 and 8 hours respectively and pipe C can empty the same tank in 12 hours. If all three pipes are opened at the same time then in how many time the tank will be filled?
questions.questionHtml: Pipe A and pipe B can fill a tank alone in 6 and 8 hours respectively and pipe C can empty the same tank in 12 hours. If all three pipes are opened at the same time then in how many time the tank will be filled?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total tank capacity = LCM(6, 8, 12) = 24 units.

Combined efficiency = (24 ÷ 6) + (24 ÷ 8) − (24 ÷ 12) = 4 + 3 − 2 = 5 units/hr.

Time taken to fill = Total capacity ÷ Combined efficiency = 24 ÷ 5 = 4.8 hours.

0.8 hours in minutes = 0.8 × 60 = 48 minutes.

∴ The correct answer is 4 hours 48 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by pipe A to fill the tank = 6 hours

Time taken by pipe B to fill the tank = 8 hours

Time taken by pipe C to empty the tank = 12 hours

Formula Used:

Total Capacity = LCM of individual times

Efficiency = Total Capacity ÷ Time

Total Time = Total Capacity ÷ Total Efficiency

Pipe Time (hrs) Total Capacity Efficiency
A (Inlet) 6 24 24 ÷ 6 = +4
B (Inlet) 8 24 ÷ 8 = +3
C (Outlet) 12 24 ÷ 12 = −2

Calculations:

⇒ Total efficiency when all pipes are open = +4 + 3 − 2 = 5 units/hr

⇒ Time required to fill the tank = 24 ÷ 5 = 4.8 hours

⇒ Converting the decimal part into minutes = 0.8 × 60 = 48 minutes

⇒ Total time required = 4 hours 48 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 4 hours 48 minutes.

Additional Information

Pipes and Cisterns Base Concept

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours, its work done per hour is +1/x. If an outlet pipe empties it in y hours, its work done per hour is −1/y.

Combined Work Rule

The net efficiency of multiple pipes operating simultaneously is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies. Inlet pipes contribute positive work, while outlet pipes represent negative work.

Time Conversion

To convert fractional or decimal hours into minutes, simply multiply the decimal fraction by 60. Example: 0.25 hours = 0.25 × 60 = 15 minutes.

questions.question: The radius of a circle with centre O is \(\sqrt{50}\) cm. A and C two points on the circle, and B is a point inside the circle. The length of AB is 6 cm, and the length of BC is 2 cm. The angle ABC is a right angle. Find the square of the distance OB.
questions.questionHtml: The radius of a circle with centre O is \(\sqrt{50}\) cm. A and C two points on the circle, and B is a point inside the circle. The length of AB is 6 cm, and the length of BC is 2 cm. The angle ABC is a right angle. Find the square of the distance OB.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Place point B at the origin (0, 0). Since ∠ABC = 90°, set A = (6, 0) and C = (0, 2).

Let center O = (x, y). Given OA2 = OC2 = 50 (radius squared).

Distance equations: (x−6)2 + y2 = 50 and x2 + (y−2)2 = 50.

Equating them: x2−12x+36+y2 = x2+y2−4y+4 ⇒ 12x − 4y = 32 ⇒ y = 3x − 8.

Solving for B inside the circle (x2+y2 < 50) gives x = 1, y = −5.

Square of distance OB = x2 + y2 = 12 + (−5)2 = 26.

∴ The correct answer is 26.

Alternate Method

 

Given:

Radius of the circle = √50 cm

AB = 6 cm, BC = 2 cm

∠ABC = 90°

Calculation:

Since ABC is a right-angled triangle,

AC = √(AB2 + BC2)

= √(62 + 22)

= √40 = 2√10

Let the coordinates of A be (0, 0).

Since O is the centre of the circle and OA = √50, let OD be the perpendicular from O to AC.

Then, AD = AC/2 = √10

Applying Pythagoras theorem in right triangle ODA,

OD = √(OA2 - AD2)

= √(50 - 10) = √40

Therefore, coordinates of O = (√10, √40).

Area of triangle ABC = (1/2) × 6 × 2 = 6 square units.

Let the height from B to AC be h.

(1/2) × AC × h = 6

(1/2) × 2√10 × h = 6

√10 × h = 6

h = 6/√10

Taking AC as the x-axis, the x-coordinate of B is

x = √(AB2 - h2)

= √(62 - (6/√10)2)

= √(36 - 36/10)

= √32.4

Hence, coordinates of B = (√32.4, 6/√10).

Distance OB = √[(√10 - √32.4)2 + (√40 - 6/√10)2]

Squaring both sides,

OB2 = (√10 - √32.4)2 + (√40 - 6/√10)2

Expanding and simplifying,

OB2 = 26

Additional Information

Equation of a Circle

For a circle with center (h, k) and radius r, any point (x, y) on the circumference satisfies (x − h)2 + (y − k)2 = r2.

Position of a Point relative to a Circle

A point P is inside if OP < r, on the boundary if OP = r, and outside if OP > r, where O is the center.

Pythagoras Theorem in Coordinate Geometry

The square of the distance between two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is given by (x2 − x1)2 + (y2 − y1)2.

questions.question: In a class of 45 students, 40% are girls and the remaining are boys. The average marks of the girls are 64 and that of the boys is 60. What is the average marks of the whole class?
questions.questionHtml: In a class of 45 students, 40% are girls and the remaining are boys. The average marks of the girls are 64 and that of the boys is 60. What is the average marks of the whole class?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Girls : Boys = 40% : 60% = 2 : 3.

Assume the base average is 60.

Deviation for Girls = 64 − 60 = +4.

Net surplus = 2 parts × (+4) = +8.

Average increase = 8 ÷ (2 + 3) = 8 ÷ 5 = 1.6.

Total average = 60 + 1.6 = 61.6.

∴ The correct answer is 61.6 marks.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total students = 45

Percentage of girls = 40% | Percentage of boys = 60%

Average marks: Girls = 64, Boys = 60

Formula Used:

Average Marks = (Total Marks of Girls + Total Marks of Boys) ÷ Total Students

Calculations:

⇒ Number of Girls = 40% of 45 = (40 ÷ 100) × 45 = 18

⇒ Number of Boys = 45 − 18 = 27

⇒ Total marks of Girls = 18 × 64 = 1152

⇒ Total marks of Boys = 27 × 60 = 1620

⇒ Total marks of class = 1152 + 1620 = 2772

⇒ Average marks of class = 2772 ÷ 45

⇒ Average marks of class = 61.6

∴ The correct answer is 61.6 marks.

Additional Information

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups are combined, the total average A = (n1a1 + n2a2) ÷ (n1 + n2), where n is the count and a is the individual average.

Deviation Method for Averages

Select an assumed average (usually the smaller value) and add the net surplus divided by the total number of items: New Avg = Assumed Avg + (Total Deviation ÷ Total Items).

Ratio impact on Averages

The average of a group depends on the ratio of the quantities, not the absolute numbers. If the total number 45 were changed to 90, the result would remain 61.6.

questions.question: Two men and 7 women can complete a work in 28 days, whereas 6 men and 16 women can do the work in 11 days. In how many days will 5 men and 4 women, working together, will complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: Two men and 7 women can complete a work in 28 days, whereas 6 men and 16 women can do the work in 11 days. In how many days will 5 men and 4 women, working together, will complete the work?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Work Equating: 28(2M + 7W) = 11(6M + 16W)

⇒ 56M + 196W = 66M + 176W ⇒ 10M = 20W ⇒ 1M = 2W

Total Work = (2 × 2 + 7 × 1) × 28 = 308 units

Required Efficiency (5M + 4W) = 5(2) + 4(1) = 14 units

Days = 308 ÷ 14 = 22 days.

∴ The correct answer is 22 days.

Alternate Method

Given: Group 1 (2M + 7W) in 28 days and Group 2 (6M + 16W) in 11 days.

⇒ Total Work = LCM(28, 11) = 308 units.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
2M + 7W 28 308 11
6M + 16W 11 28

⇒ 2M + 7W = 11 --- (i)

⇒ 6M + 16W = 28 --- (ii)

⇒ Multiplying (i) by 3: 6M + 21W = 33 --- (iii)

⇒ Subtracting (ii) from (iii): 5W = 5 ⇒ W = 1

⇒ Substituting W=1 in (i): 2M + 7 = 11 ⇒ 2M = 4 ⇒ M = 2

⇒ Efficiency of (5M + 4W) = 5(2) + 4(1) = 14 units/day

⇒ Time required = 308 ÷ 14 = 22 days.

∴ The correct answer is 22 days.

Additional Information

Work-Efficiency Relation

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. If work is constant, efficiency is inversely proportional to time.

Man-Days Concept

For multiple groups, M1D1 = M2D2 is used when the amount of work remains the same.

Combined Efficiency

When different types of workers (men, women, children) work together, their individual efficiencies are summed up to find the total rate.

questions.question: If sinθ = 0.8, then find the value of (25cosθ + 9tanθ - 1) ÷ (4cotθ - 27secθ + 1).
questions.questionHtml: If sinθ = 0.8, then find the value of (25cosθ + 9tanθ - 1) ÷ (4cotθ - 27secθ + 1).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given sinθ = 0.8 = 4/5. Using Pythagorean triplet (3, 4, 5), Base = 3.

cosθ = 3/5, tanθ = 4/3, cotθ = 3/4, secθ = 5/3.

Expression = [25(3/5) + 9(4/3) − 1] ÷ [4(3/4) − 27(5/3) + 1]

Expression = [15 + 12 − 1] ÷ [3 − 45 + 1] = 26 ÷ (−41) = −26/41.

∴ The correct answer is −26/41.

Alternate Method

Given: sinθ = 0.8

Formula Used: sinθ = P/H, cosθ = B/H, tanθ = P/B, cotθ = B/P, secθ = H/B

⇒ sinθ = 0.8 = 8/10 = 4/5

⇒ Let Perpendicular (P) = 4 units and Hypotenuse (H) = 5 units.

⇒ Base (B) = √(H2 − P2) = √(52 − 42) = √(25 − 16) = √9 = 3 units.

⇒ cosθ = B/H = 3/5

⇒ tanθ = P/B = 4/3

⇒ cotθ = B/P = 3/4

⇒ secθ = H/B = 5/3

⇒ Numerator = (25 × 3/5) + (9 × 4/3) − 1 = 15 + 12 − 1 = 26

⇒ Denominator = (4 × 3/4) − (27 × 5/3) + 1 = 3 − 45 + 1 = −41

⇒ Value = 26 / (−41) = −26/41

∴ The correct answer is −26/41.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental relations: sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ, and 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

Reciprocal Ratios

secθ = 1/cosθ, cosecθ = 1/sinθ, and cotθ = 1/tanθ.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common integer sides for right triangles include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), and (8, 15, 17).

questions.question: A man Read 5/9 of a book on 1st day, 4/5 of remaining on 2nd day, if 40 pages are still remaining. Find the total number of pages in the book
questions.questionHtml: A man Read 5/9 of a book on 1st day, 4/5 of remaining on 2nd day, if 40 pages are still remaining. Find the total number of pages in the book
questions.solution:
Given:

Read 1st day = \(\frac{5}{9}\)

Read 2nd day = \(\frac{4}{5}\) of remaining

Remaining pages = 40

Formula used:

Total pages = Total units × Value of 1 unit

Calculation:

Let total units = 9 × 5 = 45 units

1st day read = \(\frac{5}{9} \times 45\) = 25 units

Remaining after 1st day = 45 - 25 = 20 units

2nd day read = \(\frac{4}{5} \times 20\) = 16 units

Final remaining = 20 - 16 = 4 units

⇒ 4 units = 40

⇒ 1 unit = \(\frac{40}{4}\) = 10

⇒ Total pages = 45 units = 45 × 10 = 450

∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questions.question: A, B and C enter into partnership by investing capitals in the ratio \(\frac{1}{2} : \frac{1}{3}: \frac{1}{4}\) . After 4 months, A withdraws 50% of his Capital and after another 8 months, profit of ₹20240 is distributed between them. What is the difference between the shares of A and C in the profit?
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C enter into partnership by investing capitals in the ratio \(\frac{1}{2} : \frac{1}{3}: \frac{1}{4}\). After 4 months, A withdraws 50% of his Capital and after another 8 months, profit of ₹20240 is distributed between them. What is the difference between the shares of A and C in the profit?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of capitals = 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4 → 6 : 4 : 3 (multiplying by LCM 12)

A's profit units = (6 × 4) + (3 × 8) = 48 units

B's profit units = 4 × 12 = 48 units; C's profit units = 3 × 12 = 36 units

Ratio A : B : C = 48 : 48 : 36 = 4 : 4 : 3

Total 11 units = ₹20240 → 1 unit = ₹1840

Difference (A − C) = 4 − 3 = 1 unit = ₹1840

∴ The correct answer is ₹1840.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial capital ratio (A : B : C) = 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4

Total time = 12 months

Total Profit = ₹20240

Formula Used: Profit Share = Investment × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Convert fractional ratio to integer: LCM(2, 3, 4) = 12

⇒ A : B : C = (1/2 × 12) : (1/3 × 12) : (1/4 × 12) = 6 : 4 : 3

⇒ A's investment for 12 months = (6 × 4) + (50% of 6 × 8) = 24 + 24 = 48 units

⇒ B's investment for 12 months = 4 × 12 = 48 units

⇒ C's investment for 12 months = 3 × 12 = 36 units

⇒ Profit Ratio A : B : C = 48 : 48 : 36 = 4 : 4 : 3

⇒ Total Profit units = 4 + 4 + 3 = 11

⇒ 11 units = ₹20240

⇒ 1 unit = 20240 ÷ 11 = ₹1840

⇒ Difference between share of A and C = 4 units − 3 units = 1 unit

⇒ Difference = ₹1840

∴ The correct answer is ₹1840.

Additional Information

Profit Sharing Rule

In a partnership, the profit is distributed in the ratio of the product of capital invested and the time period of investment (P = I × T).

Effective Capital

If the investment changes during the period, the total effective capital is the sum of products of capital and its respective duration: Σ(Ii × Ti).

Ratio Conversion

To simplify fractional ratios like 1/a : 1/b : 1/c, multiply each term by the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the denominators a, b, and c.

questions.question: A square of side \(6\sqrt 2 \) cm is inscribed in a circle. What is the area (in cm 2 ) of the circle excluding the square (correct to the nearest integer)? (Use π = \(\frac{{22}}{7}\) )
questions.questionHtml: A square of side \(6\sqrt 2 \) cm is inscribed in a circle. What is the area (in cm2) of the circle excluding the square (correct to the nearest integer)? (Use π = \(\frac{{22}}{7}\))
questions.solution:
Diagonals of the square = \(6\sqrt{2}\) × \(\sqrt{2}\) ⇒ 12

⇒  2r = 12,  r = 6

Area of Circle = πr2 =  \(22\over7\) × 62 ⇒ \(22\over7\) × 36 ⇒ \(792\over7\)

Area of Square = (\(6\sqrt{2}\))2 ⇒ 72

Area of the circle excluding the square = Area of the circle - Area of square ⇒ \(792\over7\) - 72 ⇒ 113.14 - 72 = 41.15

questions.question: If 40% of the people read newspaper X, 50% read newspaper Y and 10% read both the newspaper, then what percentage of the people read neither of the newspaper?
questions.questionHtml: If 40% of the people read newspaper X, 50% read newspaper Y and 10% read both the newspaper, then what percentage of the people read neither of the newspaper?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total percentage of people who read at least one newspaper = Newspaper X + Newspaper Y − Both

Total readers = 40% + 50% − 10% = 80%

Percentage of people who read neither = 100% − Total readers

Neither = 100% − 80% = 20%

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Percentage of people reading newspaper X, n(X) = 40%

Percentage of people reading newspaper Y, n(Y) = 50%

Percentage of people reading both X and Y, n(X ∩ Y) = 10%

Formula: n(X ∪ Y) = n(X) + n(Y) − n(X ∩ Y)

⇒ People reading only newspaper X = 40% − 10% = 30%

⇒ People reading only newspaper Y = 50% − 10% = 40%

⇒ People reading at least one newspaper = 30% (Only X) + 40% (Only Y) + 10% (Both) = 80%

⇒ People reading neither newspaper = 100% − 80% = 20%

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Additional Information

Venn Diagram for Two Sets

For any two sets A and B, the union is given by n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B).

Complement of Union

The percentage of people who read neither is the complement of the union: n(Neither) = n(Universal Set) − n(A ∪ B).

Only Set Calculation

The number of elements in 'Only A' is n(A) − n(A ∩ B), and similarly for 'Only B'.

questions.question: A cylindrical tank of radius \(2{1\over 2}\) m and height 3 m is full of water. If 47.1 kilolitre water is taken out from the tank, then to what percent does the water level drop in the tank? (Take π = 3.14)
questions.questionHtml: A cylindrical tank of radius \(2{1\over 2}\) m and height 3 m is full of water. If 47.1 kilolitre water is taken out from the tank, then to what percent does the water level drop in the tank? (Take π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Volume (V) = πr2h = 3.14 × (2.5)2 × 3 = 58.875 m3.

Volume of water removed = 47.1 kilolitres = 47.1 m3.

Remaining Volume = 58.875 − 47.1 = 11.775 m3.

Percentage level drop to = (Remaining Volume ÷ Total Volume) × 100.

⇒ (11.775 ÷ 58.875) × 100 = 1/5 × 100 = 20%.

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius (r) = 2.5 m = 5/2 m

Height (H) = 3 m

Water removed = 47.1 kilolitres = 47.1 m3 (since 1 kl = 1 m3)

π = 3.14

Formula Used:

Volume of Cylinder = πr2h

Percentage level = (Current Height ÷ Total Height) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Base Area of tank = πr2

⇒ Base Area = 3.14 × (2.5)2 = 3.14 × 6.25 = 19.625 m2

⇒ Height of water removed (hremoved) = Volume removed ÷ Base Area

⇒ hremoved = 47.1 ÷ 19.625 = 2.4 m

⇒ New water level height = Total Height − Height removed

⇒ New height = 3 − 2.4 = 0.6 m

⇒ Percentage drop to = (New height ÷ Total height) × 100

⇒ Percentage drop to = (0.6 ÷ 3) × 100

⇒ Percentage drop to = 0.2 × 100 = 20%

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Additional Information

Volume of a Cylinder

The volume of a cylinder with radius r and height h is given by V = πr2h.

Kilolitre and Cubic Meter Relationship

1 kilolitre (kl) is exactly equal to 1 cubic meter (m3). 1 litre = 1000 cm3.

Percentage Level in Uniform Cross-section

For a tank with a uniform base (like a cylinder or prism), the percentage of volume is directly proportional to the percentage of height.

questions.question: If \(\rm a+\frac{1}{a}=4\) , then what is the value of \(\rm a-\frac{1}{a}?\)
questions.questionHtml: If \(\rm a+\frac{1}{a}=4\), then what is the value of \(\rm a-\frac{1}{a}?\)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Direct Identity: (a − 1/a) = √[(a + 1/a)2 − 4]

Given: a + 1/a = 4

Substitute: √[42 − 4] = √[16 − 4] = √12

Simplify: √12 = 2√3

∴ The correct answer is 2√3.

Alternate Method

Given: a + 1/a = 4

Formula Used: (x + y)2 − (x − y)2 = 4xy

⇒ Let x = a and y = 1/a

⇒ (a + 1/a)2 − (a − 1/a)2 = 4 × a × (1/a)

⇒ (a + 1/a)2 − (a − 1/a)2 = 4

⇒ (4)2 − (a − 1/a)2 = 4

⇒ 16 − (a − 1/a)2 = 4

⇒ (a − 1/a)2 = 16 − 4

⇒ (a − 1/a)2 = 12

⇒ a − 1/a = √12

⇒ a − 1/a = √(4 × 3)

⇒ a − 1/a = 2√3

∴ The correct answer is 2√3.

Additional Information

Square Reciprocal Relation

If x + 1/x = k, then x2 + 1/x2 = k2 − 2. Conversely, if x − 1/x = k, then x2 + 1/x2 = k2 + 2.

Cubic Reciprocal Relation

If x + 1/x = k, then x3 + 1/x3 = k3 − 3k. If x − 1/x = k, then x3 − 1/x3 = k3 + 3k.

Direct Conversion Rule

To convert (x + 1/x) to (x − 1/x) directly, use (x − 1/x) = √[(x + 1/x)2 − 4]. To convert (x − 1/x) to (x + 1/x), use (x + 1/x) = √[(x − 1/x)2 + 4].

Step - 1 - Parts of an equation enclosed in 'Brackets' must be solved first,

Step - 2 - Any mathematical 'Of' or 'Exponent' should be solved next,

After interchanging, the equation becomes,

The correct answer is '1' i.e. The research fellowship committee only intends to grant three additional stipends .

Key Points

  • The error in the sentence lies in the placement of the word "only." Its incorrect position changes the intended meaning of the sentence.
  • The word "only" should be placed immediately before the word or phrase it modifies to avoid ambiguity.
  • The corrected sentence should read: The research fellowship committee intends to grant only three additional stipends.

Correct sentence: The research fellowship committee intends to grant only three additional stipends to doctoral candidates whose work focuses on renewable energy storage, despite the fact that over two hundred applications were submitted by highly qualified researchers from across the globe.

Additional Information

  • Correct Usage of "Only":
    • When "only" is misplaced, it can cause confusion or unintended meanings.
    • Example of misplaced "only": She only eats chocolate on weekends. (Implies that she does not do anything else with chocolate.)
    • Correct placement: She eats chocolate only on weekends. (Clarifies that eating chocolate happens exclusively on weekends.)

Additional Information

  • Subjunctive Mood:
    • The subjunctive mood is used to express demands, suggestions, or hypothetical situations.
    • In such cases, the base form of the verb is used (e.g., "be" instead of "is").
    • Example: "It is crucial that she attend the meeting."
  • Indicative Mood:
    • In contrast, the indicative mood is used to express factual statements or questions.

  • Option 2 incorrectly uses the past tense ("was circumstantial" and "was entitled") in direct speech, which is not appropriate for quoting the judge's exact words.
  • Options 3 and 4 rephrase the sentence but do not accurately reflect the original wording of the given sentence.

Correct sentence: The judge said, "The evidence against the accused is circumstantial; he is, therefore, entitled to the benefit of the doubt.".

Additional Information

  • Direct Speech: In direct speech, the exact words spoken are enclosed in quotation marks. For example: She said, "I am happy."
  • Indirect Speech: In indirect speech, the speaker's words are reported without quotation marks, often involving changes in tense and pronouns. For example: She said that she was happy.

Key Points

  • The provided sentence is in Passive Voice, and our objective is to convert it to Active Voice.
  • The given sentence is in the past continuous tense.

  • The structure of the conversion is as follows:

    • Active: [Subject] + was/were + [verb+ing] + [object].
      Example: "The dog was chasing the mailman."

    • Passive: [Object] + was/were + being + [past participle of verb] + by + [subject].
      Example: "The mailman was being chased by the dog."​

  • Hence, for the given sentence, the general structure for switching from Passive to Active voice involves transforming the format from 'Object + was being + Verb(V3) + by + Subject' (Passive Voice) to 'Subject + was (indicative of past continuous tense) + Verb(V1) + Object' (Active Voice).
  • Here, 'the appraiser' is the subject and 'the antique clock' is the object.
  • We will change the positions of the subject and object, and also adjust the verb according.
  • In this case, 'was being carefully examined by' becomes 'was examining carefully'.
  • Thus, the sentence in Active voice is 'The appraiser was examining the antique clock carefully'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

  • The option 'You always come lately to class.' is incorrect.

    • Therefore, 'lately' should be replaced with 'late'.
  • The option 'She loves to be called Maa by her sister's daughters.' is correct.
    • Don't use as with >> name, elect, think, consider, call, appoint, make, choose.
    • Use as with >> regard, describe, define, treat, view, know
  • The option 'The demise of Mr. Raghavan surprised no one terribly other than Raghu.' is incorrect.
    • We have to use the comparative form of an adverb in the given sentence.

    • So, here hardly is a negative word, remove not.
    • Therefore, 'I did not know hardly anyone' should be replaced with 'I hardly knew anyone'.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is 'She loves to be called Maa by her sister's daughters.'


The correct sentence- She loves to be called Maa by her sister's daughters.

  • An adverb is a word/a set of words that modifies verbs, adjectives, and other adverbs. It tells when, where, and how an action is performed or indicates the quality or degree of the action.

  • Adverb Clauses and Adverb Phrases are clauses and phrases that modify the verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs in the sentence.

    • Sentence Adverbs

  • Impact:

questions.question: Which of the following films is considered the first Indian sound (talkie) film, marking the beginning of Bollywood?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following films is considered the first Indian sound (talkie) film, marking the beginning of Bollywood?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Alam Ara.

Key Points

  • Alam Ara (1931) was the first Indian sound film, marking the beginning of the "talkie" era in Indian cinema.
  • Directed by Ardeshir Irani, Alam Ara was released on 14 March 1931. It was a milestone in Indian cinema and paved the way for the Bollywood industry.
  • The film featured dialogue and songs, making it revolutionary compared to silent movies that existed before. Hence, Alam Ara is considered the first Indian talkie film.
  • Raja Harishchandra, made by Dadasaheb Phalke in 1913, was India's first full-length silent feature film. It does not qualify as the first sound film. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.
  • Sholay (1975) and Mughal-e-Azam (1960) were significant films in Indian cinema but were not the first sound films. Hence, statements 1 and 4 are incorrect.
  • Alam Ara featured seven songs and introduced playback singing in Indian cinema. The song "De de khuda ke naam par" sung by Wazir Mohammed Khan became iconic.
  • The film's themes revolved around royal intrigue, love, and family drama, setting a precedent for Bollywood's storytelling style. Hence, statement 3 is correct.

Additional Information

  • Alam Ara:
    • Production: Alam Ara was produced by Imperial Movietone. Ardeshir Irani used the Tantra system to record sound, which was cutting-edge technology at the time.
    • Plot: The story revolved around a love triangle between a prince, a gypsy girl, and a princess. It included themes of romance, betrayal, and conflict.
    • Impact: Alam Ara inspired the production of sound films across India, creating a shift from silent cinema to talkies.
  • Raja Harishchandra:
    • Directed by: Dadasaheb Phalke, considered the "Father of Indian Cinema".
    • Release: 1913, it marked the beginning of Indian cinema but was a silent film.
    • Significance: It laid the foundation for India's film industry but did not feature sound.
  • Sound in Indian Cinema:
    • The advent of sound films brought new opportunities for Indian cinema, including dialogue, playback singing, and sound effects.
    • Example: Alam Ara set the tone for Bollywood's musical and dramatic themes.

Important Points

  • Technological Advancements:
    • Sound Recording: Alam Ara was recorded using the Tanar system, which was the first sound recording technology used in India.
    • Playback Singing: The concept of playback singing was introduced, which later became a hallmark of Indian cinema.
  • Legacy of Alam Ara:
    • The film is no longer available as the prints of Alam Ara were destroyed. However, it remains a crucial part of Indian cinematic history.
    • Recognition: Alam Ara is remembered as the first Indian sound film, a pioneer in integrating sound and storytelling.

questions.question: Choose the correct sequence of embryonic development in humans:
questions.questionHtml: Choose the correct sequence of embryonic development in humans:

options.html: Fertilization → Zygote → Cleavage → Morula → Blastocyst

questions.solution:
In humans, fertilization occurs in the ampullary-isthmic junction of the fallopian tube to form a zygote. The zygote undergoes mitotic divisions (cleavage) to create 2, 4, 8, and 16-celled stages. The 8-16 celled embryo is called a morula, which continues to divide to form the blastocyst. Therefore, the correct sequence of embryonic development in humans is as follows:

Fertilization → Zygote → Cleavage → Morula → Blastocyst.

questions.question: Identify the bacterium which is inserted into a crop plant to provide resistance to pests from following options.
questions.questionHtml: Identify the bacterium which is inserted into a crop plant to provide resistance to pests from following options.
questions.solution:
Concept:

  • Biological control or biocontrol is the use of the naturally occurring enemies of insects, pests, and other disease-causing agents to control and eliminate them.
  • Microbes like bacteria, fungi, viruses, etc. are used as biocontrol agents.
  • Biocontrol agents have three modes of action - cause disease to the pest, compete with them or kill them.
  • The biocontrol agents are multiplied on artificial media.
  • These artificially grown agents are then released in large numbers to control the pest population naturally.
  • This process is called augmentative biological control.

Explanation:

  • Bacillus typhimurium - 
    • ​Salmonella typhimurium is a bacillus i.e. a rod-shaped bacteria.
    • It is a pathogenic bacteria found in the intestinal lumen.
    • It causes gastroenteritis in mammals including humans.
    • It is not used as a biocontrol agent.
  • Bacillus taiwanensis - 
    • ​Bacillus taiwanensis is a Gram-positive bacteria. 
    • It was isolated first from a soil sample in Taiwan.
    • It is known to be a non-human pathogenic organism.
    • It is not used as a biocontrol agent.
  • ​​Bacillus thuringiensis - 
    • ​Bacillus thuringiensis is a biocontrol agent.
    • It is used in agriculture to control the population of caterpillars and butterflies.
    • Bacillus thuringiensis controls the population of pests by killing them.
    • Bt crops such as cotton, brinjal,etc. are genetically engineered crops that contain the cry gene isolated from Bacillus thuringiensis. 
    • This gene encodes a toxin that is insecticidal in  property.
  • Bacillus tropicus - 
    • ​Bacillus tropicus is a Gram-positive rod-shaped bacteria.
    • It was first isolated from the sediments of the South China Sea.
    • Studies have shown that Bacillus tropicus has the ability to biodegrade low density polyethylene (LDPE).
    • Polyethylene is the most commonly used plastic.
    • It is not used as a biocontrol agent.

So the correct answer is option 3 (Bacillus thuringiensis).​

questions.question: Which is the highest layer of the atmosphere in which Meteors burn up after entering Earth's atmosphere?
questions.questionHtml: Which is the highest layer of the atmosphere in which Meteors burn up after entering Earth's atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mesosphere.

 

  • Mesosphere:
    • This is the highest layer of the atmosphere in which the gases are all mixed up rather than being layered by their mass.
    • Meteors burn up in this layer after entering Earth's atmosphere and before reaching Earth's surface.
    • The meteors make it through the exosphere and thermosphere without much trouble because those layers don’t have much air. 
    • But when they hit the mesosphere, there are enough gases to cause friction and create heat.

Additional Information

  • Troposphere:
    • The troposphere is the innermost layer of Earth’s atmosphere.
    • This layer gets its name from the weather that is constantly changing and mixing up the gases in this part of our atmosphere.
    • This layer has the air we breathe and the clouds in the sky. 
  • Stratosphere:
    • The stratosphere is located above the troposphere and below the mesosphere.
    • There are no storms or turbulence here to mix up the air, so cold, heavy air is at the bottom and warm, light air is at the top. 
    • The ozone layer found in this stratosphere helps protect us from ultraviolet radiation (UV) from the sun by blocking UV radiations from reaching the Earth’s surface.
    • The ozone layer absorbs most of the UV radiation sends to us by the sun.
  • Thermosphere:
    • The thermosphere is located above the mesosphere and below the exosphere.
    • The thermosphere is home to the International Space Station as it orbits Earth.

  • The Council of States, or Rajya Sabha, is composed of not more than 250 members as stated in the Constitution of India.
  • Statement B is incorrect. The President of India nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha for their contributions to arts, literature, science, and social service. The field of sports is not explicitly mentioned in the Constitution.
  • The process of election of members from the States and Union Territories involves proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote, which is the same across the States and Union Territories.
  • However, Option C is partially incorrect because the election process slightly varies between States and Union Territories due to differing numbers of representatives.
  • Members of Rajya Sabha (Upper House) from states are elected by the elected MLAs of that state’s Legislative Assembly using the proportional representation system with a single transferable vote.
  • Some Union Territories (like Delhi and Puducherry) have Legislative Assemblies, and their Rajya Sabha members (if applicable) are elected similarly to states.
  • Other UTs, which do not have Legislative Assemblies (like Chandigarh, Lakshadweep), do not elect Rajya Sabha members.

Additional Information

    • The Lok Sabha, or House of the People, is the lower house of India's bicameral Parliament.
    • It is composed of representatives directly elected by the people of India.
    • The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552 members.
  • Legislative Assembly
    • Each state in India has its own Legislative Assembly, which is the lower house of the state's legislature.
    • Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) are directly elected by the people of the state.
    • The number of MLAs varies from state to state depending on the population.
  • Legislative Council
    • Some states in India also have a Legislative Council, which is the upper house of the state's legislature.
    • Members of the Legislative Council (MLCs) are elected through various methods, including by MLAs, graduates, teachers, and local authority members.
    • Not all states in India have a Legislative Council; it exists only in a few states.

questions.question: Consider the following statements about Fundamental Duties: 1. It is the duty of every citizen to protect public property. 2. Defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so. 3. Fundamental Duties are listed in Part III of the Indian Constitution. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statements about Fundamental Duties:

1. It is the duty of every citizen to protect public property.

2. Defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.

3. Fundamental Duties are listed in Part III of the Indian Constitution.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 Only.

Key Points

  • Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution and were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
  • Initially, there were 10 duties, but in 2002, the 86th Amendment added an 11th one, which emphasizes education for children.
  • These duties aren't enforceable by law but serve as moral obligations for every citizen to promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India. 🇮🇳
  • It includes respecting the National Flag, cherishing the heritage of India, and protecting the environment. 
  • Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution were inspired by the Soviet Union's Constitution.

Additional Information

  • The DPSP, enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, serves as guidelines for the State to formulate policies aimed at achieving socio-economic justice and promoting the welfare of the people.
  • The DPSP in India closely mirrors the principles laid out in the Constitution of Ireland.
  • Article 39: It ensures adequate means of livelihood and equal pay for equal work, promoting a sense of responsibility among citizens towards national development.
  • Article 40: Provides for the organization of village panchayats for local self-governance.
  • Article 47: Directs the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health.
  • Panchayati Raj Day is celebrated in India on April 24th each year.

Important PointsDifferences Between Fundamental Duties and DPSP

  • Fundamental Duties: It is non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced in a court of law.
  • DPSP: It is also non-justiciable, but it provides a framework for making laws and policies aimed at social welfare.
  • Fundamental Duties: It focuses on the responsibilities of citizens towards the nation.
  • DPSP: It focuses on the responsibilities of the State to ensure justice and equality for its citizens.

Similarities Between Fundamental Duties and DPSP

  • Non-justiciability: Both are non-justiciable provisions in the Constitution, meaning they cannot be legally enforced in courts.
  • Aim for National Development: Both aim to promote the welfare of the country—Fundamental Duties encourage citizen participation, while DPSP guide the State’s policies for achieving social and economic justice.

questions.question: What does SUMIF function do in Microsoft Excel ?
questions.questionHtml: What does SUMIF function do in Microsoft Excel ?

options.text: Adds up cell values based on a condition
options.html: Adds up cell values based on a condition

options.text: Adds all the numbers in a range of cells
options.html: Adds all the numbers in a range of cells

options.text: Returns a subtotal in a list or database
options.html: Returns a subtotal in a list or database

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Adds up cell values based on a condition

Key Points

  • SUMIF Function: ✅ The SUMIF function in Microsoft Excel adds the values in a range that meet a specified condition (criteria). It combines the summing and conditional logic in one function.
  • Adds All Numbers: ❌ The function to add all the numbers in a range of cells without conditions is called SUM, not SUMIF.
  • Returns a Subtotal: ❌ The function that returns a subtotal in a list or database is called SUBTOTAL, not SUMIF.

Additional Information

  • Syntax: The syntax for SUMIF is =SUMIF(range, criteria, [sum_range]), where:
    • Range: The range of cells to evaluate for the condition.
    • Criteria: The condition to be applied (e.g., ">=10").
    • Sum_range (optional): The range of cells to sum if the condition is met. If omitted, Excel sums the cells in the range.
  • Example: =SUMIF(A1:A10,">10",B1:B10) adds the values in B1:B10 where the corresponding cells in A1:A10 are greater than 10.
  • Common Applications: The SUMIF function is widely used for financial analysis, sales reports, inventory management, and other scenarios where conditional summation is needed.

Hence, the correct answer is: option 1) Adds up cell values based on a condition

Key PointsVirtualization uses software to create an abstraction layer over computer hardware that allows the hardware elements of a single computer processor, memory, storage, and more to be divided into multiple virtual computers, commonly called virtual machines (VMs). Each VM runs its own operating system (OS) and behaves like an independent computer, even though it is running on just a portion of the actual underlying computer hardware.

It is a technology that lets you create useful IT services using resources that are traditionally bound to hardware.
